receipt_kinds.when_produced: Default Rust SDK output (no compression requested) in the 1.x era. Contains the per-segment STARK receipts for the whole session plus auxiliary receipts resolving execution assumptions (segment exit-code assumption and the po2/circuit-size assumption). Not recommended for third-party or on-chain verification because the recipient must re-verify the whole segment chain and assumption resolution. Field layout changed materially between 0.x (SegmentReceipt{index, po2, seal, hashfn}, no per-segment claim) and 1.x (segments carry claims/exit-code receipts); do not assume one shape across versions.
receipt_kinds.caveat: Exact CompositeReceipt field names (seal, assumption_receipts, exit_code_receipt, journal_digest/claim_digest) are 1.x-era and may have shifted in 2.x/3.x; I am least sure of this variant's exact struct.

receipt_kinds.when_produced: After running the risc0 recursion pipeline (lift/join/resolve over segments): a single STARK receipt whose circuit verifies the whole computation's final ReceiptClaim. Seal is a large Poseidon-based STARK proof; claim is a full ReceiptClaim; carries control ids (input/output control digests in 1.x, naming version-dependent) that the verifier must match against the control root of its trusted circuit set.

Compression of the Succinct receipt: the succinct STARK's verification is re-proven inside a Groth16 circuit over BN254 (circom-based stark-to-snark). Produced via risc0's groth16 prover when the user requests the compressed form; intended for cheap on-chain verification (Ethereum verifier contracts hardcode the Groth16 verifying key, control root, and bn254 control id). Introduced in the 1.0 line; does not exist in 0.x.

groth16_receipt_fields.type_shape: Raw Rust form: 256 bytes of Groth16 proof (pi_a G1 64B, pi_b G2 128B, pi_c G1 64B on BN254). ABI/Ethereum form: 592 bytes = 256B proof plus ~336B of receipt material (the serialized ReceiptClaim, 208B / 52 words, and the 4 public-input limbs: claim digest split into two 128-bit limbs + control root + bn254 control id, 128B). Exact ordering/offsets of the non-proof bytes vary by risc0-ethereum release; treat offsets as release-specific.
groth16_receipt_fields.meaning: The cryptographic proof; everything else in the receipt is metadata the seal must commit to.
groth16_receipt_fields.verifier_must_check: Validate proof points are canonical (coordinates < field modulus, on-curve, correct subgroup, not point-at-infinity) before the pairing check; recompute the claim digest from the claim bytes carried in the seal (sha256 over the serialized claim) rather than trusting any digest field; check the recomputed digest equals the public-input limbs; check control root and bn254 control id equal the constants bound to the deployed verifying key; then run the pairing check.
groth16_receipt_fields.failure_if_skipped: If canonicality/on-curve checks are skipped, degenerate or malleated proofs (e.g., point-at-infinity or non-canonical coordinate encodings) can be crafted so a 'valid' seal exists without knowledge of a real proving key. If the claim digest is taken from a seal field instead of recomputed, an attacker swaps in a claim for a different program/exit code with the same journal digest and it passes.

groth16_receipt_fields.type_shape: ReceiptClaim: 52 words / 208 bytes in 1.x serialization (pre and post SystemState of 17 words each, 1-word exit code, 8-word input digest, 9-word optional output digest). In the Rust struct it embeds the journal for Groth16Receipt<Journal>; in the OuterReceipt the journal bytes sit outside.
groth16_receipt_fields.meaning: The statement being proven: which program, what input, what final memory state, how it exited, and the journal commitment.
groth16_receipt_fields.verifier_must_check: Recompute sha256 over the serialized claim and compare to the public-input digest limbs; extract pre.digest (image ID) and output (journal digest) and compare against the caller/app's expected values; check exit_code is the one the application accepts (normally Halted(0)).
groth16_receipt_fields.failure_if_skipped: Skipping the image-ID comparison lets a receipt for a different guest program vouch for your journal; skipping the exit-code check lets a paused/split or errored execution (Halted(nonzero), Paused, SystemSplit) be presented as a completed successful run.

groth16_receipt_fields.type_shape: Digest (32B sha256-style in the Rust VerifiersConfig) encoding the root of the Merkle tree of control IDs for all sanctioned recursion circuits; on BN254 it is carried as a single field element (encoding from digest to field element is version-dependent and flagged as uncertain).
groth16_receipt_fields.meaning: Pins the exact set of circuits (segment/lift/join/resolve) that may appear inside the proof chain.
groth16_receipt_fields.verifier_must_check: Verify the seal's control root equals the one the verifier's own parameters/verifying key were generated for (in Solidity it is a compile-time constant; in Rust the DefaultVerifier embeds it).
groth16_receipt_fields.failure_if_skipped: An attacker proves execution with their own modified circuit set whose control tree they computed themselves, producing a seal that internally verifies while asserting an arbitrary claim — total forgery with a real-looking receipt.

groth16_receipt_fields.type_shape: Digest identifying the bn254 stark-to-snark wrapper circuit; carried as a single BN254 field element among the public inputs.
groth16_receipt_fields.meaning: Identifies which wrapper circuit the Groth16 verifying key corresponds to; ties the SNARK to a specific risc0 release's circuits.
groth16_receipt_fields.verifier_must_check: Must equal the constant associated with the hardcoded Groth16 verifying key; a mismatch means the seal was produced for a different circuit than the key being used.
groth16_receipt_fields.failure_if_skipped: If a deployer wires a verifying key from release A with control ids from release B (or accepts a caller-supplied control id), proofs from an unvetted circuit version verify; conversely honest receipts from the intended version are rejected or, worse, a matching attacker circuit/key pair is accepted.

groth16_receipt_fields.type_shape: Raw bytes, carried alongside the inner receipt, not inside the seal.
groth16_receipt_fields.meaning: The guest's committed output; the seal never contains the journal itself, only its digest in claim.output.
groth16_receipt_fields.verifier_must_check: Compute sha256(journal_bytes) and require it equals claim.output; do this on every verify, not only at creation.
groth16_receipt_fields.failure_if_skipped: Journal substitution: any valid receipt can be repackaged with arbitrary journal bytes, so an attacker shows your image ID with a fabricated result.

components.pre: SystemState { pc: u32, merkle_root: Digest, digest: Digest } — machine state before the proven span; digest field is the image ID (sha256-style digest of the guest ELF), merkle_root is the root of the memory Merkle tree.
components.post: SystemState, same shape, at the end of the span; for a final receipt the merkle_root is the final memory commitment.
components.exit_code: ExitCode enum: SystemSplit | Halted(u8) | Paused; Halted(0) is the normal successful halt; Paused/SystemSplit relate to session continuation and are what 'verify' must distinguish from a finished run.
components.input: Digest — commitment to the guest input (added in 1.x; not present in 0.x claims).
components.output: Option<Digest> — Some(sha256(journal)) for a completed run; serialized as 8 digest words plus a 1-word present/none marker (exact marker encoding version-dependent).

claim_structure.digest_computation: The claim is serialized word-aligned via the Digestible/bytemuck path (52 words / 208 bytes in 1.x, including the Option marker) and hashed with sha256; Receipt::claim_digest() / ReceiptClaim::digest() return this value. The Groth16 public inputs carry this digest split into two ~128-bit limbs to fit the BN254 scalar field. Any change in claim fields or serialization across versions changes this digest, so digests are not comparable across risc0 versions.
claim_structure.uncertainty: Word-level offsets and the Option<Digest> marker value are reconstructed from the 1.x layout and the 592-byte ABI seal arithmetic (256+208+128=592); confirm against the specific release before relying on byte offsets.

binding_chain: 1. journal bytes -> sha256 -> journal digest; the VM records it as claim.output for a completed session.
2. ReceiptClaim assembled: pre.digest = image ID (program), pre/post.merkle_root = memory roots, exit_code, input digest, output = journal digest.
3. claim serialized (52 words) -> sha256 -> claim digest; this single 256-bit value is the canonical statement identifier.

4. Segment STARKs prove spans; the recursion pipeline (lift/join/resolve) produces a Succinct receipt whose proof internally checks that every consumed proof's control ID is a leaf of the control tree with root = control_root. This is where the control root enters: it is the whitelist of circuits, enforced in-circuit.

5. The Groth16 (bn254 control id) circuit verifies the succinct STARK and exposes public inputs: [claim digest limbs, control root, bn254 control id]. The bn254 control id ties the SNARK itself to the sanctioned wrapper circuit.

6. Seal = Groth16 proof (+ claim + public inputs in the ABI form). Verifier: recompute claim digest from claim bytes, match limbs, match control constants against verifying-key-bound values, pair-check, then bind to application data: claim.pre.digest == expected image ID, sha256(journal) == claim.output, exit_code acceptable.
Key invariant: the journal is bound only through claim.output inside the claim digest; nothing else in the seal touches the journal bytes.

circuit_version_dependent: Control root and all control IDs: derived from the recursion circuit set, they change with each risc0 release (0.x and 1.x are incompatible; 1.x point releases also changed them).
Groth16 verifying key, SEAL_SIZE, and the CONTROL_ROOT/BN254_CONTROL_ID constants hardcoded in the Ethereum verifier contract — all correspond to one release.
ReceiptClaim serialization layout (field set, Option marker) — changes shift the claim digest for identical semantics.
Segment/composite receipt shapes (0.x SegmentReceipt without claims vs 1.x claim-bearing segments).
2.x/3.x-era additions such as verifier-parameter/anchor mechanisms were introduced after my most confident knowledge; treat their specifics as unverified.
what_breaks_with_wrong_version: Benign failure: honest receipts from release A fail verification under release B's control root / verifying key — availability breaks, not safety.

Safety break: if a verifier is loosened to 'accept multiple control roots' or takes control constants from the receipt itself, an attacker proves with an attacker-built circuit set and forges arbitrary claims.
Digest confusion: claim digests computed under different serializations are incomparable; caching or comparing digests across versions misattributes results.
ABI confusion: parsing a seal with another release's offsets silently reads garbage as the claim, so recomputed digests and image-ID checks fail in confusing ways rather than cleanly.

common_verifier_bugs.bug: Trusting a journal digest carried in the seal/API instead of hashing the journal bytes and comparing to claim.output on every verify.
common_verifier_bugs.catching_check: require(sha256(journal_bytes) == claim.output) inside the verify path, computed from the actual bytes presented.

common_verifier_bugs.bug: Not validating exit code — accepting Paused, SystemSplit, or Halted(nonzero) as a completed successful commitment.
common_verifier_bugs.catching_check: require(claim.exit_code == Halted(0)) for final receipts; only continuations-oriented code may accept Paused/SystemSplit, and then it must resolve the continuation explicitly.

common_verifier_bugs.bug: Accepting receipts with unresolved assumptions (composite receipts whose assumption receipts do not resolve, or continuation receipts presented as final).
common_verifier_bugs.catching_check: Reject any receipt whose claim still references unresolved assumptions; verify assumption resolution when consuming Composite receipts.

common_verifier_bugs.bug: Recomputing the claim digest as sha256(imageId || journalDigest) or otherwise from a partial claim, instead of sha256 over the full serialized ReceiptClaim.
common_verifier_bugs.catching_check: Recompute the digest over the complete claim bytes as serialized by the matching risc0 version and compare against the public-input limbs.

common_verifier_bugs.bug: Skipping BN254 canonicality checks on proof points (coordinates in range, on-curve, subgroup, non-infinity) before the pairing check.
common_verifier_bugs.catching_check: Explicit on-curve and field-range validation of pi_a/pi_b/pi_c, or use a verifier implementation known to enforce it, so malleated/degenerate proofs cannot verify.

common_verifier_bugs.bug: Hardcoding or wiring control root / verifying key from a different risc0 release than the one that produced receipts (or 'supporting' several roots to make errors go away).
common_verifier_bugs.catching_check: Pin one release: assert the seal's control root and bn254 control id equal the constants bound to the deployed verifying key, and regenerate both together when upgrading the guest toolchain.

certainty_notes.receipt_kinds: High confidence that Composite/Succinct/Groth16 are the 1.x inner receipt variants and when each is produced; exact CompositeReceipt field names are medium confidence and likely shifted in 2.x.
certainty_notes.groth16_receipt_fields: Field names seal/claim/verifiers_config(control_root, bn254_control_id) are from the 1.x risc0-zkvm design with medium-high confidence; the 592-byte ABI seal total is well-attested, but the internal byte ordering (proof/claim/limbs) is reconstructed from size arithmetic (256+208+128) and is medium-low confidence — verify offsets against the risc0-ethereum release you target.
certainty_notes.claim_structure: High confidence on the field set (pre/post SystemState with pc, merkle_root, digest=image ID; exit_code variants; input; output Option) and sha256-based Digestible digest; medium confidence on the 52-word size and the Option<Digest> marker encoding.
certainty_notes.binding_chain: High confidence on the chain's shape (journal->output digest, claim digest as public input, control root as circuit whitelist enforced in-circuit, VK pinning the wrapper); medium confidence on the exact limb split of the claim digest and the digest-to-BN254-field-element encoding.
certainty_notes.version_coupling: High confidence that control root/control IDs/VK/claim serialization are release-coupled and that mismatched versions fail benignly while loosened checks enable forgery; low confidence on specific 2.x/3.x verifier-parameter mechanisms.
certainty_notes.common_verifier_bugs: Journal-check omission, exit-code omission, control-root pinning, and non-canonical point issues are known classes in risc0-adjacent verification; the unresolved-assumptions and partial-claim-digest bugs are plausible constructions labeled as such rather than documented incidents.
